translations.text: Josiah fathered Jeconiah and his brothers at the time of the exile to Babylon.
All this happened so that what the Lord had spoken through the prophet would be fulfilled.
They said, “In Bethlehem of Judea, for this is what is written in the prophet.”
He came and lived in a town called Nazareth, so that what was spoken through the prophets would be fulfilled: “He will be called a Nazarene.”
I baptize you with water for repentance, but the one coming after me is stronger than I am. I am not worthy to carry his sandals. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.
When Jesus was baptized, he immediately came up out of the water. The heavens were opened to him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and coming upon him.
He opened his mouth and taught them, saying:
For truly I tell you, until heaven and earth pass away, not one letter yod or one stroke will pass away from the Law until everything happens.
But when you give to the poor, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing.
The eye is the lamp of the body. Therefore, if your eye is sound, your whole body will also be full of light.
Therefore, do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Each day has enough trouble of its own.
For you will be judged by the judgment you use, and you will be measured by the measure you use.
Another of his disciples said to him, “Lord, let me first go and bury my father.”
His disciples came up and woke him, saying to him, “Our Lord, save us! We are perishing!”
He said to them, “Go away, for the girl is not dead but asleep.” And they laughed at him.
But they went out and spread the news about him throughout that whole region.
When Jesus saw the crowds, he had compassion on them, because they were weary and lying helpless, like sheep without a shepherd.
No disciple is greater than his teacher, nor is a servant greater than his master.
Are not two sparrows sold for a small coin? Yet not one of them falls to the ground apart from your Father.
Whoever loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me, and whoever loves son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.
The blind see, the lame walk, those with leprosy are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead rise, and the poor receive good news.
But Jesus knew their thoughts and said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself will be laid waste, and every house [?] and city divided against itself will not stand.”
And whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken from him. This is why I speak to them in parables: because they see but do not see, and hear but do not hear or understand.
He said to them, “An enemy has done this.” His servants said to him, “Do you want us to go and gather them?”
He came to his own town and taught them in their synagogues, so that they were astonished and said, “Where did this man get this wisdom and these mighty deeds?”
For Herod had seized John, bound him, and put him in prison because of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip.
But she, having been instructed by her mother, said, “Give me John the Baptist’s head here on a platter.”
He sent and had John’s head cut off in prison.
His disciples came, took his body, and buried it. Then they came and told Jesus.
Jesus said to them, “Bring them here to me.”
During the fourth watch of the night, Jesus came to them, walking on the water.
Jesus answered them, “Why do you yourselves also violate God’s commandment because of your tradition?”
Jesus said to them, “How many loaves do you have?” They said to him, “Seven, and a few small fish.”
But he said to them, “Watch out! Beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
When Jesus came to the region of Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, “Who do people say that I, the Son of Man, am?”
They said, “Some say John the Baptist, others Elijah, and others Jeremiah or one of the prophets.”
He said to him, “Lord, have mercy on me! My son has epilepsy and suffers terribly. He often falls into the fire and often into the water.”
“Whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble would be better off having a donkey-driven millstone hung around his neck and being drowned in the depths of the sea.”
“For the Son of Man came to save what was lost.”
“Again I tell you, if two of you on earth agree about anything they ask for, it will be done for them by my Father in heaven.”
“For wherever two or three are gathered in my name, I am there among them.”
“So they are no longer two, but one body. Therefore, what God has joined together, no human being should separate.”
But he said to them, “Not everyone can accept this saying, but only those to whom it has been given.”
Jesus looked at them and said to them, “For human beings this is impossible, but for God everything is possible.”
But he answered one of them, “Friend, I am not treating you unjustly. Didn’t you agree with me on a denarius?”
Two blind men were sitting beside the road. When they heard that Jesus was passing by, they cried out, “Have mercy on us, Lord, Son of David!”
They answered him, “We don’t know.” Jesus said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.”
“But concerning the resurrection of the dead, haven’t you read what God said to you when he said,”
When the crowds heard this, they were amazed at his teaching.
“For the Lord said to my Lord, ‘Sit at my right hand until I put your enemies beneath your feet.’”
And do not call anyone on earth your father, for you have one Father, who is in heaven.
And you say, “If we had lived in the days of our ancestors, we would not have joined them in shedding the blood of the prophets.”
Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those sent to you! How often I wanted to gather your children together, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were unwilling!
Then those who are in Judea should flee to the mountains.
For just as lightning comes from the east and is visible as far as the west, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.
Therefore stay awake, because you do not know at what hour your Lord is coming.
But the wise ones took oil in containers along with their lamps.
His master answered him, “You wicked and lazy servant! You knew that I reap where I did not sow and gather where I did not scatter.”
For I was hungry, and you gave me food; I was thirsty, and you gave me a drink; I was a stranger, and you took me in.
Then they too will answer, “Our Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and not serve you?”
And when Jesus had finished all these words, he said to his disciples,
“You know that in two days it will be Passover, and the Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified.”
And the Son of Man goes as it is written about him, but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would have been better for that man if he had not been born.
But after I rise, I will go ahead of you to Galilee.
Jesus said to him, “Truly I tell you, tonight, before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times.”
And he said to them, “My soul is sorrowful to the point of death. Stay here for me and keep watch with me.”
And he came again and found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy.
And immediately he approached Jesus and said, “Greetings, Rabbi!” and kissed him.
But Jesus said to him, “Is this what you came for, my friend?” Then they approached, laid their hands on Jesus, and seized him.
And one of those with Jesus stretched out his hand, drew his sword, struck the high priest’s servant, and cut off his ear.
And they said, “Prophesy to us, Messiah! Who was it that struck you?”
For this reason that field has been called the Village of Blood to this day.
And as they went out, they found a man from Cyrene named Simon. They forced him to carry his cross.
And when they had crucified him, they divided his clothes by casting lots.
But some of those standing there, when they heard it, said, “This man is calling Elijah.”
And they came out, and after his resurrection they entered the holy city and appeared to many people.
Now Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were there, sitting opposite the tomb.
